title: Focus on Data Centers: Barger, Verobish Tackle Tough Issues at Joint Event
raw_text:
Focus on Data Centers: Barger, Verobish Tackle Tough Issues at Joint Event
September 24, 2026
ALTOONA –
Reps. Scott Barger (R-Blair/Huntingdon) and Andrea Verobish (R-Blair) today hosted an informational meeting about the anticipated proliferation of data centers across the United States, with a particular focus on how large-scale installations will impact the 13-state power grid that includes Pennsylvania.
Barger and Verobish addressed 200 constituents at the Blair County Convention Center, where they acknowledged concerns they’ve heard about environmental permitting, power and water usage, and the local controls established in statewide zoning laws.
Both representatives support the Ratepayer Protection Act – initiatives at both the state and federal level to ensure developers bring their own sources of new electric generation and meet other benchmarks.
“Sometimes it feels as if data center planning is outpacing sources of reliable information about the centers themselves. I’m thankful we could hold this meeting to share vetted, trustworthy information with our friends and neighbors,” Barger said.
“This next wave of development will require an all-hands-on-deck approach to ensure it is done responsibly,” Verobish said. “State lawmakers like us play a role, as do our partners in the federal government and local municipalities. Innovation and foresight are needed now more than ever.”

title: Verobish to Host Car Seat Safety Event this Wednesday
raw_text:
Verobish to Host Car Seat Safety Event this Wednesday
September 21, 2026
BLAIR – Parents and guardians of young children are invited to have their car seats checked for safety and proper installation at Rep. Andrea Verobish’s (R-Blair) child safety seat inspection event this Wednesday, Sept. 23.
The event, which is completely free, will be held from 3-6 p.m. at the AAA Altoona office, located at 1634 Valley View Blvd. in Altoona. Certified technicians will be on-site to inspect individual car seats and check if they are fit for use.
Verobish is hosting the event in partnership with PennDOT, AAA and Pennsylvania State Police.
“Parents will invest in good, high-quality car seats for their infants and toddlers so they are safe and secure in a vehicle. But installing these seats correctly is a huge part of making sure kids are fully protected on the road,” Verobish said. “As a parent of two young girls myself, my goal with this event is to help give parents some peace of mind while they are driving with their children, and give them a few tips about installing these seats you might not be able to read in a manual.”
Participants are encouraged to bring their child, safety seats, vehicle manuals and safety seat manuals when possible.
Anyone with questions should contact Verobish’s district office at 814-946-7218.
Representative Andrea Verobish
79th District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

title: Verobish: Blair County Bridge Memorializes Cousins from Altoona Who Fought in World War II
raw_text:
Verobish: Blair County Bridge Memorializes Cousins from Altoona Who Fought in World War II
September 18, 2026
BLAIR
– One of Blair County’s most traveled bridges was renamed today in honor of Jack and Sheldon Chambers, two cousins from Altoona who fought and died in World War II, following a bridge dedication ceremony held by Rep. Andrea Verobish (R-Blair).
The bridge, which is now named the Jack E. and Sheldon L. Chambers Memorial Bridge, carries Interstate 99 over Pennsylvania Route 36 (Logan Boulevard).
Jack E. Chambers enlisted in the U.S. Marine Corps in June 1942 at the age of 17. He quickly achieved the rank of corporal with the 3rd Amphibian Tractor Battalion, III Amphibious Corps, Fleet Marine Force. In July 1944, while in command of an Amphibian Tractor crew during the landing of assault troops on Guam, Jack Chambers was killed by hostile fire after helping rescue troops from nearby loaded vehicles that were incapacitated by enemy mortars. Jack Chambers was 20 years old when he died, and he is buried in the National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific in Hawaii.
Sheldon L. Chambers enlisted in the U.S. Army Air Force in June 1939 after graduating from Altoona High School. He served as a flight officer/co-pilot in the 308th Bomber Group, Heavy, 425th Bomber Squadron. In January 1944, Sheldon Chambers was part of the B-24J Liberator #42-73308, nicknamed “Hot as Hell.” When the crew took member took off from China during a routine flight to India, they were reported missing. The wreck of “Hot as Hell” was discovered in India in December 2006. Sheldon was 23 years old when he died, and he is memorialized at the Tablets of the Missing at Manila American Cemetery in the Philippines
“Jack and Sheldon joined the United States military as soon as they could, leaving the only home they had ever known. Even the remains of these brave cousins never made it back to Altoona,” Verobish said. “I am so proud we finally have a special piece of Blair County to remember Jack and Sheldon by. This landmark will remind everyone we are fortunate to call our communities home because of the service and sacrifice of our veterans, and inspire the future generation of heroes like Jack and Sheldon.”
Representative Andrea Verobish, 79th District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

Lcook@pahousegop.com

title: Verobish: Bridge Dedication this Friday Recognizes Cousins from Altoona Who Fought in World War II
raw_text:
Verobish: Bridge Dedication this Friday Recognizes Cousins from Altoona Who Fought in World War II
September 16, 2026
BLAIR – Rep. Andrea Verobish (R-Blair) invites Blair County residents and local media to attend a bridge dedication ceremony this Friday, Sept. 18, where a Blair County bridge will be renamed to honor Jack and Sheldon Chambers, cousins from Altoona who fought in World War II.
The dedication will begin at 1 p.m at Lakemont Park (700 Park Ave., Altoona), Pavillion #7. The bridge, which will formally be named the Jack E. and Sheldon L. Chambers Memorial Bridge after Friday’s ceremony, carries Interstate 99 over Logan Boulevard.
“On behalf of my office and the families of Jack and Sheldon, I’d like to personally invite all residents to this incredibly meaningful ceremony,” Verobish said. “These brave cousins each received several awards from the United States for their services and sacrifices during World War II. This is one way we can say thank you from Blair County. I hope the bridge being named in their honor inspires generations of heroes, like them, for as long as it stands.”
Jack E. Chambers enlisted in the United States Marine Corps in June 1942 at the age of 17. He quickly achieved the rank of corporal, 3rd Amphibian Tractor Battalion, III Amphibious Corps, Fleet Marine Force. In July 1944, while in command of an Amphibian Tractor crew during the landing of assault troops on Guam, Jack was killed by hostile fire after helping rescue troops from nearby loaded vehicles that were incapacitated by enemy mortars. He was 20 years old.
Sheldon L. Chambers enlisted in the United States Army Air Force in June 1939 at the age of 18. He served as a flight officer/co-pilot in the 308th Bomber Group, Heavy, 425th Bomber Squadron. In January 1944, Sheldon was part of the B-24J Liberator #42-73308, nicknamed “Hot as Hell.” When the crew took off from China during a routine flight to India, the crew was reported missing and declared dead a day later. The wreck of “Hot as Hell” was located in India in December 2006.
Jack is buried at the National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific in Hawaii. Sheldon is buried at the Manila American Cemetery and Memorial Manila in the Philippines.
“Jack and Sheldon are buried in completely different spots thousands of miles away from Blair County. I am so proud we can finally recognize them in their hometown,” Verobish said.
Anyone with questions is encouraged to contact Verobish’s Altoona district office at 814-946-7218.
Representative Andrea Verobish
79th District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

In January 1944, Sheldon was part of the B-24J Liberator #42-73308, nicknamed “Hot as Hell.” When the crew took off from China during a routine flight to India, the crew was reported missing and declared dead a day later. The wreck of “Hot as Hell” was located in India in December 2006.
Jack is buried at the National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific in Hawaii. Sheldon is buried at the Manila American Cemetery and Memorial Manila in the Philippines.
“Jack and Sheldon are buried in completely different spots thousands of miles away from Blair County. I am so proud we can finally recognize them in their hometown,” Verobish said.
Anyone with questions is encouraged to contact Verobish’s Altoona district office at 814-946-7218.

title: Verobish, Policy Committee Highlight Impact of Rising Energy Costs on Pennsylvania Businesses
raw_text:
Verobish, Policy Committee Highlight Impact of Rising Energy Costs on Pennsylvania Businesses
September 2, 2026
ALTOONA
—Rising energy costs are limiting business growth, straining workers, and driving up the price of goods throughout Pennsylvania, employers and industry leaders testified Thursday during a House Republican Policy Committee hearing hosted by Rep. Andrea Verobish (R-Blair).
The hearing, “Keeping Pennsylvania Moving: Addressing the Rising Cost of Energy,” was held at Ward Transport and Logistics Corp. in Altoona. Testifiers included Bill Ward Jr., president and CEO of Ward Transport and Logistics; Richard Weyant, facilities maintenance manager at Shirley’s Cookie Company; and Stephanie Catarino Wissman, executive director of API Pennsylvania.
“Pennsylvania has an incredible energy advantage. We have abundant natural resources, a skilled workforce, and along tradition of powering our nation with energy,” Verobish said. “We should ask ourselves why a state with so many energy resources can't do more to ensure affordable, reliable energy for people who live there.”
Verobish has authored a proposal as part of the House Republican “Lights On, Costs Down” energy package, a series of 11 bills intended to increase energy production, improve reliability and lower costs. Her legislation would establish a grid maintenance fee on electricity transported through Pennsylvania to other states and use the revenue to provide reliability credits for electricity consumed within the Commonwealth.
Ward explained that higher energy costs ultimately return to the transportation industry through the rising price of vehicles, equipment, electricity and other necessities.
“Essentially, the tools we need to move America and Pennsylvania forward are becoming more and more expensive,” Ward said. “This reduces our margins and makes it difficult to provide exceptional benefits and pay raises for all employees.”
Ward also described the pressure higher gasoline, heating and consumer prices place on employees. Those financial pressures can lead workers to seek higher wages, change jobs or take second jobs, while employers face significant costs to recruit and train their replacements.
Weyant testified that Shirley’s Cookie Company used less electricity in June 2026 than it did during the same period in 2022, yet its monthly electric bill increased by more than $7,000. That increase came despite the company investing hundreds of thousands of dollars in LED lighting, more efficient HVAC systems and other energy-saving improvements.
“The problem is that the increases in the cost of electricity outweigh any savings we are trying to make from these investments,” Weyant said.
Higher operating costs also leave the company with less money for employee compensation, equipment, automation and expansion. Weyant said Shirley’s currently has approximately $500,000 in automation projects on hold amid uncertainty surrounding electricity and fuel costs.
“We can't just pass every increase on to our customers. We compete with manufacturers from other states and other countries. Our customers have a choice,” Weyant said. “Many of these increases must be absorbed by us as a business.”
Wissman testified that Pennsylvania possesses the resources needed to meet rising demand but needs additional pipelines, power plants, natural gas storage and other infrastructure to deliver that energy reliably and affordably. She also called for more predictable permitting processes, regulatory certainty, and policies protecting consumers’ ability to choose the energy sources that best meet their needs.
“Affordability depends on a reliable energy supply,” Wissman said. “Pennsylvania can't lower costs if we make it harder to produce…the energy on which our economy depends.”
Rep. Josh Kail (R-Beaver/Washington), who spearheaded the package of “Lights On, Costs Down” legislation, emphasized that energy affordability affects the entire economy.
“What we must always remember is that it all comes back to the accessibility of energy, because the lower the cost of energy, the lower the cost of everything else,” Kail said.
Verobish said testimony from the businesses demonstrated how energy expenses ripple throughout Pennsylvania’s economy before ultimately reaching consumers.
“We all face these issues in our personal lives, but hearing businesses explain how these challenges affect our economy and how these prices are passed on to consumers, we are in a vicious circle from which we must escape,” Verobish said. “I am committed to working with my team to make this happen, so we can free up these resources and make Pennsylvania a better place to live, work and develop.”

youtube.com/@pahousegop
.

title: Verobish Invites Residents to Collect Their Unclaimed Property
raw_text:
Verobish Invites Residents to Collect Their Unclaimed Property
August 25, 2026
BLAIR
– More than one in 10 Pennsylvanians are owed unclaimed property, and Rep. Andrea Verobish (R-Blair) hopes to connect those in the 79th District with what is rightfully theirs at her unclaimed property event on Thursday, Sept. 17.
The event, hosted in partnership with the Pennsylvania Department of Treasury, will be held from 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. at Verobish’s district office,
2301 Beale Ave., Suite A in Altoona
.
“Everything in the Pennsylvania Treasury’s vault belongs to someone, and that person deserves to have it,” Verobish said. “This is a great opportunity for all residents to check to see if they have unclaimed property. If so, they can finally bring it home.”
Unclaimed property can be anything from old bank accounts, uncashed paychecks, insurance payments and more.
The Pennsylvania Department of Treasury receives hundreds of millions of dollars in unclaimed property every year. The average claim is more than $1,000.
No registration is required. Anyone with questions is encouraged to call the Altoona district office at 814-946-7218. More information about Verobish’s upcoming events can be found on her website at
RepVerobish.com/Events
.
Representative Andrea Verobish
79th District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

title: Verobish, Barger to Answer Questions about Data Centers
raw_text:
Verobish, Barger to Answer Questions about Data Centers
August 17, 2026
ALTOONA
– Reps. Andrea Verobish (R-Blair) and Scott Barger (R-Blair/Huntingdon) will host an informational meeting about data centers Thursday, Sept. 24, from 6:30-8 p.m. at the
Blair County Convention Center
.
The representatives intend to share a presentation about the state’s preparation for the projected influx of data centers, with a specific focus on the centers’ power needs. They will answer questions after the initial presentation.
“Every day, we read a new headline about data center development somewhere in Pennsylvania,” Barger said. “Lawmakers are considering several proposals that affect that development. In particular, there is bipartisan agreement these developers need to provide their own sources of electricity.”
“Regardless of where these centers are built, they have the potential to greatly impact our regional power grid. Our constituents are rightfully concerned about these centers being incorporated into Pennsylvania via smart, deliberate development,” Verobish said.
Barring technical difficulties, the informational meeting will be livestreamed at both RepBarger.com and RepVerobish.com.
Those planning to attend at the convention center, 1 Convention Center Drive in Altoona, are asked to RSVP by Sept. 18 by visiting either representative’s website and clicking the “events” tab on the top. The RSVP form includes an opportunity to submit a question for the event.
